);

            if (error_detected) begin

            end else if (command_received) begin
                status <= 3'b010; // Set Busy, clear Ready and Error

Design a simple ARQ (Automatic Repeat reQuest) protocol in Verilog that uses a stop-and-wait mechanism. The circuit should have an input for the data bit, an input for acknowledgment (ACK), and an output for the transmitted data bit. The circuit should retransmit the data bit if the ACK is not received within a certain condition (e.g., after one clock cycle).
code:
module ARQ (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire data_in,
    input wire ack,
    output reg data_out
);
    reg [1:0] state; // 0: Idle, 1: Send, 2: Wait for ACK

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            state <= 0;
            data_out <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                0: begin // Idle
                    if (data_in) begin
                        data_out <= data_in;
                        state <= 1; // Move to Send state
                    end
                end
                1: begin // Send
                    if (ack) begin
                        state <= 0; // Return to Idle
                    end else begin
                        state <= 2; // Move to Wait for ACK state
                    end
                end
                2: begin // Wait for ACK
                    if (ack) begin
                        state <= 0; // Return to Idle
                    end else begin
                        data_out <= data_out; // Retransmit
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Create a simple 2-bit branch predictor that predicts whether a branch will be taken or not based on the previous two outcomes. The predictor will maintain a 2-bit history (00, 01, 10, 11) to make predictions. The outputs should be a predicted outcome (0 for not taken, 1 for taken) and the actual outcome that updates the history.
code:
module branch_predictor (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input actual_outcome, // 0 for not taken, 1 for taken
    output reg predicted_outcome // Prediction output
);
    reg [1:0] history; // 2-bit history

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            history <= 2'b00; // Reset history
            predicted_outcome <= 0; // Default prediction
        end else begin
            // Prediction logic based on history
            case (history)
                2'b00: predicted_outcome <= 0; // Strongly not taken
                2'b01: predicted_outcome <= 0; // Weakly not taken
                2'b10: predicted_outcome <= 1; // Weakly taken
                2'b11: predicted_outcome <= 1; // Strongly taken
            endcase
            
            // Update history based on actual outcome
            if (actual_outcome) begin
                if (history < 2'b11) 
                    history <= history + 1; // Increment history towards "taken"
            end else begin
                if (history > 2'b00) 
                    history <= history - 1; // Decrement history towards "not taken"
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

module watchdog_timer (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [3:0] timeout, // Timeout period
    output reg output_signal
);
    reg [3:0] counter;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin

            output_signal <= 1'b0; // Reset output signal

It should support a maximum of N blocks, where N is defined as a parameter. The allocator will store the status (allocated or free) of each block and provide the following functionality:

2. `free`: Deallocate a previously allocated block.
3. `status`: Return the status of all blocks.
The memory blocks will be indexed from 0 to N-1. The output of the memory status should show which blocks are allocated and which are free.

module memory_allocator #(parameter N = 8) (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire [2:0] cmd, // 0: malloc, 1: free, 2: status
    input wire [2:0] index, // index for malloc/free
    output reg [N-1:0] mem_status // memory status output
);
    reg [N-1:0] mem_array;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            mem_array <= {N{1'b0}}; // Initialize all blocks to free (0)
            mem_status <= {N{1'b0}};
        end else begin
            case (cmd)
                3'b000: begin // malloc
                    if (index < N && mem_array[index] == 1'b0) begin
                        mem_array[index] <= 1'b1; // Allocate the block
                    end
                end
                3'b001: begin // free
                    if (index < N) begin
                        mem_array[index] <= 1'b0; // Deallocate the block
                    end
                end
                3'b010: begin // status
                    mem_status <= mem_array; // Output the memory status
                end
                default: begin
                    mem_status <= mem_status; // No action
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

module uart_transmitter (
    input wire clk,             // Clock input
    input wire reset,           // Asynchronous reset
    input wire [7:0] data_in,   // Data to transmit
    input wire start_tx,        // Start transmission signal
    output reg tx,              // UART transmit output
    output reg tx_done          // Transmission done signal
);

    reg [3:0] bit_index;        // Bit index for transmission
    reg [9:0] tx_shift_reg;     // Shift register for transmission
    reg transmitting;           // Indicates if currently transmitting

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            tx <= 1;              // Idle state for UART is high
            tx_done <= 0;
            bit_index <= 0;
            transmitting <= 0;
        end else begin
            if (start_tx && !transmitting) begin
                // Load the shift register with start bit, data, and stop bit
                tx_shift_reg <= {1'b1, data_in, 1'b0}; // Stop bit is high (1)
                transmitting <= 1;
                bit_index <= 0;
                tx_done <= 0;
            end else if (transmitting) begin
                if (bit_index < 10) begin
                    tx <= tx_shift_reg[0]; // Transmit the LSB
                    tx_shift_reg <= tx_shift_reg >> 1; // Shift right
                    bit_index <= bit_index + 1;
                end else begin
                    tx_done <= 1; // Transmission complete
                    transmitting <= 0;
                    tx <= 1; // Idle state
                end
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

    input wire clk,
    input wire load,
    input wire [7:0] parallel_in,
    output reg serial_out,
    output reg done
);

    reg [2:0] count;

        if (load) begin
            shift_reg <= parallel_in; // Load data
            count <= 3'b000;          // Reset count
            done <= 1'b0;             // Not done yet
        end else if (count < 3'b111) begin
            serial_out <= shift_reg[7]; // Shift out the MSB
            shift_reg <= {shift_reg[6:0], 1'b0}; // Shift left
            count <= count + 1;         // Increment count

Design a JK flip-flop in Verilog that takes inputs J, K, clock, and reset. The flip-flop should toggle its output Q based on the following conditions:

    output reg Q  
);

        else begin

);

);

        if_reg <= operand1; // assuming operand1 as instruction

    // Instruction Decode stage
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        id_reg <= if_reg; // pass instruction to next stage

module serializer(
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input load,
    input [7:0] data_in,
    output reg serial_out
);
    reg [2:0] bit_counter; // 3 bits to count from 0 to 7
    reg [7:0] shift_reg;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            bit_counter <= 3'b0;
            serial_out <= 1'b0;
            shift_reg <= 8'b0;
        end else if (load) begin
            shift_reg <= data_in; // Load input data
            bit_counter <= 3'b0; // Reset bit counter
        end else if (bit_counter < 3'd8) begin
            serial_out <= shift_reg[7]; // Output the MSB first

Design a digital Kalman filter that takes in a noisy measurement and an estimated state. The filter has to compute the updated state and the error covariance. The inputs to the filter will be the measurement (z), the estimated state (x_hat), the process noise covariance (Q), the measurement noise covariance (R), and the state transition matrix (A) and measurement matrix (H). The output will be the updated state (x_hat_new) and updated error covariance (P_new).
code:
module kalman_filter (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire [15:0] z,        // Measurement
    input wire [15:0] x_hat,    // Estimated state
    input wire [15:0] Q,        // Process noise covariance
    input wire [15:0] R,        // Measurement noise covariance
    input wire [15:0] A,        // State transition matrix
    input wire [15:0] H,        // Measurement matrix
    output reg [15:0] x_hat_new, // Updated state
    output reg [15:0] P_new     // Updated error covariance
);

    reg [15:0] P;               // Error covariance

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            x_hat_new <= 16'b0;
            P_new <= 16'b0;
            P <= 16'b1; // Initial error covariance
        end else begin
            // Prediction update
            x_hat_new <= A * x_hat; // Updating the state
            P <= A * P * A + Q;      // Update the error covariance

            // Measurement update
            P_new <= P * H / (H * P * H + R); // Update the error covariance
            x_hat_new <= x_hat_new + P_new * (z - H * x_hat_new); // Update the state
        end
    end
endmodule

                count <= count + 1; // Increment counter

                pulse_out <= 0; // Set output low
                if (count < (pulse_width + pulse_width)) begin

module ARQ_System (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [3:0] data_in,
    input wire ack_in,
    output reg [3:0] data_out,
    output reg ack_out,
    output reg retransmit
);
    reg [1:0] state; // 0: Idle, 1: Send, 2: Await Ack, 3: Retransmit

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= 0;
            ack_out <= 0;
            retransmit <= 0;
            data_out <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                0: begin // Idle state
                    data_out <= data_in;
                    ack_out <= 0;
                    retransmit <= 0;
                    state <= 1;
                end
                1: begin // Send state
                    ack_out <= 1; // Acknowledge data sent
                    state <= 2;
                end
                2: begin // Await Acknowledgment
                    if (ack_in) begin
                        ack_out <= 0; // Clear ack_out
                        state <= 0; // Go back to Idle state
                    end else begin
                        retransmit <= 1; // Need to retransmit
                        state <= 3; // Move to retransmit state
                    end
                end
                3: begin // Retransmit state
                    data_out <= data_in; // Resend the data
                    ack_out <= 1; // Re-acknowledge sending
                    state <= 2; // Go back to Await Ack
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

Design a simple 2-bit branch predictor using a 2-bit saturating counter. The predictor should output whether the branch is predicted to be taken or not taken based on its current state. The state transitions are as follows:  
- From state 00 (Strongly Not Taken) to 01 (Weakly Not Taken) on a Not Taken input, and to 10 (Weakly Taken) on a Taken input.  
- From state 01 (Weakly Not Taken) to 00 on Not Taken and to 10 on Taken.  
- From state 10 (Weakly Taken) to 01 on Not Taken and to 11 (Strongly Taken) on Taken.  
- From state 11 (Strongly Taken) to 10 on Not Taken and remains in 11 on Taken.  
The output should be 1 if the prediction is Taken (state 10 or 11) and 0 if Not Taken (state 00 or 01). The initial state should be 00.
code:
module branch_predictor (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input taken, // 1 for Taken, 0 for Not Taken
    output reg prediction // 1 for Taken, 0 for Not Taken
);
    reg [1:0] state;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            state <= 2'b00; // Initial state
        end else begin
            case (state)
                2'b00: state <= taken ? 2'b10 : 2'b00; // Strongly Not Taken
                2'b01: state <= taken ? 2'b10 : 2'b00; // Weakly Not Taken
                2'b10: state <= taken ? 2'b11 : 2'b01; // Weakly Taken
                2'b11: state <= taken ? 2'b11 : 2'b10; // Strongly Taken
            endcase
        end
    end

    always @(*) begin
        prediction = (state[1] == 1); // Taken if state is 10 or 11
    end
endmodule

);

    reg [3:0] block_count; // current number of allocated blocks

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            allocated_memory <= 16'b0;
            block_count <= 4'b0;
        end else if (allocate) begin
            if (block_count < 16 && request_size <= 16) begin
                allocated_memory <= allocated_memory | (1 << block_count); // allocate block
                block_count <= block_count + 1;
            end
        end else if (free) begin
            if (block_count > 0 && free_size < block_count) begin
                allocated_memory <= allocated_memory & ~(1 << free_size); // free block
                block_count <= block_count - 1;
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

Design a simple Kalman filter in Verilog that estimates the state of a system given noisy measurements. The system will have the following parameters:
- State variable (x): a 16-bit signed integer
- Measurement variable (z): a 16-bit signed integer
- Process noise (q): a 16-bit signed integer
- Measurement noise (r): a 16-bit signed integer
- The Kalman gain (K), predicted state (x_pred), and estimated state (x_est) should be computed in a clocked process.
code:
module kalman_filter (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input signed [15:0] z, // Measurement
    input signed [15:0] q, // Process noise
    input signed [15:0] r, // Measurement noise
    output reg signed [15:0] x_est // Estimated state
);
    reg signed [15:0] x_pred; // Predicted state
    reg signed [15:0] P; // Estimate error covariance
    reg signed [15:0] K; // Kalman gain

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            x_est <= 0;
            P <= 16'hFFFF; // initial large uncertainty
        end else begin
            // Prediction step
            x_pred <= x_est; // assuming no control input
            P <= P + q; // Increase uncertainty due to process noise

            // Update step
            K <= P / (P + r); // Kalman gain
            x_est <= x_pred + K * (z - x_pred); // Update estimate
            P <= (16'hFFFF - K) * P; // Update uncertainty
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a Voltage-Controlled Oscillator (VCO) in Verilog which generates a square wave output that toggles between high and low states based on the control voltage input. The frequency of the output signal should increase with an increase in the control voltage. The VCO should have a configurable frequency range and should be implemented using a counter and a clock.
code:
module vco (
    input wire clk,                 // Clock input
    input wire [7:0] control_voltage, // Control voltage (from 0 to 255)
    output reg vco_out             // VCO output
);
    reg [31:0] counter;            // Counter to determine output frequency
    reg [31:0] toggle_time;        // Time period to toggle the output

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        // Calculate toggle_time based on control_voltage
        toggle_time <= (255 - control_voltage) * 1000; // Scale for frequency range
        
        if(counter >= toggle_time) begin
            vco_out <= ~vco_out;    // Toggle output
            counter <= 0;           // Reset counter
        end else begin
            counter <= counter + 1; // Increment counter
        end
    end
endmodule

module watchdog_timer(
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input signal_in,
    output reg timeout
);
    parameter TIMEOUT_PERIOD = 10; // Timeout period in clock cycles
    reg [3:0] counter; // 4-bit counter to count clock cycles

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            counter <= 0;
            timeout <= 0;
        end else if (signal_in) begin
            counter <= 0; // Reset the counter when signal_in is high
            timeout <= 0;
        end else if (counter < TIMEOUT_PERIOD) begin
            counter <= counter + 1; // Increment counter
            timeout <= 0;
        end else begin
            timeout <= 1; // Set timeout if counter reaches the timeout period
        end
    end
endmodule
